title: Nanzhao
capsule: Nanzhao was a Tai-Bai polity centered on the Erhai Lake basin in present-day Yunnan, China, that rose under Piluoge (r. 728–748), who unified six rival zhao chieftainships with Tang sponsorship and established the capital at Taihe. At its height the kingdom extended from the Red River valley into Burma and pressed Tang China hard enough to repel three major Tang military expeditions between 750 and 754, inflicting tens of thousands of casualties. The dynasty passed through successive name-changes — Dameng, Dali, Dafengmin — before the line was extinguished when power minister Zheng Maisi supplanted the ruling Meng clan and proclaimed the Datang (Great Tang) kingdom in 902. The polity's territory became the foundation of the Kingdom of Dali, which persisted until Mongol conquest in 1253.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately attested via Tang annals and later Dali-kingdom stele inscriptions, but precise boundary years remain disputed among scholars of Yunnanese history.
